personalHistory: Male, about 45, 180 cm; last confirmed body weight 93 kg (2026-08-04); recently reports 1–2 kg gained but not weighed at a specified date.
Gym 3 core sessions weekly plus optional fourth, strength development focused on chest and biceps; regular steps reported around 10k daily.
Lactose intolerance; occasional bloating; prefers a sustainable plan over calorie counting.
Familiar foods: eggs, tuna tomato pasta, chicken, salmon, rice, pasta, potatoes, rye bread, dark chocolate; social meals/travel matter.
Prior reports of dizziness around workouts: avoid training long-fasted, support with food and fluids.
sourceProvenance.confidence: Older 2026 documents are historical proposals, not verified medical instructions; quantities here are new planning estimates. No current scale trend, dietary recall, labs, food allergies, or measured calorie expenditure were supplied.
corrections: A two-scoop post-workout shake is optional, not mandatory.
More than 40 g protein in one meal is not wasted; daily intake matters most.
Meal timing is flexible; no mandatory breakfast within one hour of waking.
Salt and cortisol do not automatically explain belly fat; bloating and weight trends need observations.
Do not infer exact calories in restaurant meals.

goal.primary: Support resistance training, preserve/build muscle, gradually improve waist without a strict diet

proteinTargetG.note: Flexible daily range. Older user preference was 130–150 g. At ~93 kg, ~140–160 g is a practical compromise consistent with the broad 1.4–2.0 g/kg sports-nutrition range for healthy exercising adults.

goal.calories: No fixed calorie prescription until a 14-day weight/waist and food-intake baseline is available. Do not imply numbers in recipes are precise.
goal.mealStructure: Usually 3 main meals + 1 snack or shake; switch timing around work, travel and hunger.
goal.hydration: Drink consistently; ~2–3 L total fluids/day is a flexible starting point, adjust for heat, sweat and thirst; do not force 3 L as medical rule.

guidelines: Use plate portions, not compulsive tracking: per main meal ~1–2 palm portions protein, one fist vegetables (or two at lunch/dinner), one fist carbohydrate; training days can use an additional carb portion when needed, especially before or after lifting.
Include protein at breakfast, lunch, dinner and usually one protein-rich snack; a shake is optional if a meal is short on protein.
For afternoon lifting: have a meal with protein and carbohydrate 1–3 h before; if several hours have passed and you are hungry, add fruit and a small protein snack.
No immediate post-workout deadline: eat dinner or a normal protein-rich meal in the hours after exercise; shake only if convenient.
Keep lactose-free products as the default. Avoid default whey concentrate, normal milk and regular cottage cheese when they trigger symptoms.
No blanket elimination of onion, gluten, beans or sodium. If bloating is frequent, log timing and possible triggers for 2 weeks before making targeted changes.
Dark chocolate stays as an option: begin with ~20–30 g rather than unmeasured handfuls, but not a forbidden food.
One flexible social dinner per week is built in. Work trips and late meetings use flexible swaps without shame or compensatory fasting.
Use varied protein sources including fish 2–3 times per week, poultry, eggs and legumes as tolerated; canned tuna is not the default every day.
If fatigue, dizziness, severe bloating or new GI symptoms recur, pause strenuous exercise or seek medical review as appropriate.

trainingDayHints.preWorkout: If last full meal was 3–4 hours ago, consider a banana + lactose-free skyr or a small sandwich 30–90 minutes before training.
trainingDayHints.postWorkout: A normal dinner with 30–45 g protein is sufficient. Optional 1 scoop lactose-free whey isolate if convenient.
carbAdditions: 40–60 g extra dry rice/pasta in a meal

restDayHints.protein: Keep protein similar to training days; there is no need to intentionally cut it.
restDayHints.carbs: Use normal appetite; you may want slightly less rice/pasta on sedentary days, but no forced restrictions.

bloatingExperiment.instructions: Use waist at belly-button level consistently, morning after bathroom. Record 2–3 weights weekly if wanted. Look for patterns, not one-day fluctuations. Recurrent persistent or painful distension merits medical discussion.

adjustmentRules.condition: After 2–3 weeks, morning waist trends down slowly and strength/energy are steady
After 2–3 weeks, waist and average bodyweight both trend upward and user wants a leaner waist
adjustmentRules.action: Reduce ONE optional energy-dense extra per day (e.g. 20–30 g nuts, a large added sauce or one extra carb portion); keep protein and training meals.

adjustmentRules.condition: Weight is dropping quickly or gym performance/sleep/hunger worsen
adjustmentRules.action: Add an extra carbohydrate serving around workouts and reassess recovery; do not automatically cut further.

adjustmentRules.condition: Bloating varies strongly with dairy or a specific food
adjustmentRules.action: Try a focused lactose-free or portion adjustment and observe, rather than broad elimination.
